quote: Last, loneliest, loveliest, exquisite, apart— / On us, on us the unswerving season smiles, / Who wonder ’mid our fern why men depart / To seek the Happy Isles!
source: Rudyard Kipling, A Song of the English, The Song of the Cities, the Auckland stanza, The Seven Seas (Methuen, 1896)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg text of The Seven Seas (ebook 27870), transcribed from the D. Appleton and Company printing, copyright 1896; fetched and read this run
evidence.edition: The Seven Seas, 1896 (Methuen, London; Appleton, New York, same year and text)
evidence.locator: A Song of the English, section The Song of the Cities, the stanza headed Auckland

reason: The four lines stand verbatim under the heading Auckland in The Song of the Cities, a section of A Song of the English, with the dash after apart and the exclamation at Happy Isles. Kipling stands at one of three (month 5) and is not banned; shipped.js finds no match. The Happy Isles are the Isles of the Blessed, so a place thanking its season and doubting the search for paradise elsewhere carries both halves of the theme. The source now names the parent poem the section belongs to.
